Small numbers fight the speckle; white numbers with an outline or a plate read well.
Almost nothing: the micro tiles already fill the surface
Pairs well with: chrome, black, deep purple, silver.
pitfalls: Not a chrome flake: the picture is coloured matte-ish shards, not silver
Not a quasicrystal Penrose tiling you can see: the shapes are too small, they read as shards
Avoid: small numbers over sparkle, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 77 (pearl-level metal), roughness 162 (matte or blasted), clearcoat 112 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over sparkle, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing: the micro tiles already fill the surface; a plain plate or stripe band for numbers
Patterns to avoid: any fine pattern, grid or flake: noise on noise and muddy
Spec overlays that work: clean gloss lift in the black gaps for depth; avoid glitter, the shards already do that
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

examples.title: Put it on a zone
examples.goal: See Penrose Reactor on the car.
examples.result: The finish shows its own colours and spec together.
